HomeAll projectsBrowser Automation System

AI / BROWSER WORKFLOWS

Make browser-agent runs inspectable.

A task dashboard around a browser agent, with execution records that help explain what happened during a run.

ProjectBrowser Automation System
ScopePublic experimental application
StackPython · FastAPI · React · browser-use · WebSockets

The problem

A natural-language instruction can start a browser task, but it does not explain the run's progress or failure. Experimentation needs visible execution history and a way to carry useful context into another attempt.

My contribution

  • Connected natural-language task creation to AI analysis and browser-use execution.
  • Built a React dashboard with WebSocket progress updates and execution history.
  • Added stored checkpoints, screenshots, reported token usage and pattern suggestions from prior runs.

How the system works

Task descriptionAI analysisBrowser runProgress & historyReview

Separate orchestration from the interface. FastAPI coordinates execution while React handles task creation and review. REST and WebSockets connect the two.

Retain context for another attempt. Checkpoints preserve execution context rather than claiming to save a live browser session.

Keep experiments observable. JSON records hold tasks, history and patterns so the execution flow can be inspected during development.

What you can verify

The public repository contains the application, setup instructions and implementation notes. It demonstrates task orchestration, browser-agent integration and a live progress interface.

Source repositoryImplementation notes

Scope & limitations

This is an experimental application. Saved patterns do not guarantee better outcomes, and checkpoints do not resume an exact live browser state. The backend has no built-in authentication and should remain local unless access controls are added.
